full_judgment: Although prosecution is saddled with the burden of proving the case to its entirety, section 106 of the Evidence Act is an exception to the general rule and also to section 101 of the Evidence Act. Section 106 lays down that any fact which is within the knowledge of any person, that person alone is to discharge the onus of proving that fact. For instance: A was taken to the house of B. A was subsequently found dead with injuries on his person. The character and circumstances of the death of A suggest that B killed A. B is therefore required to rebut the presumption that he is not responsible for killing A. B is furthered required to prove the nature and cause of 'A's death. Where the subject matter of the allegation lies peculiarly within the knowledge of one of the parties, that party must prove it. When a person does an act with some intention other than that which the character and circumstance of the case suggest, it is not for the prosecution to eliminate all other possible intentions. If the accused had a different intention, that is a fact especially within his knowledge. He is to prove such special knowledge on fact.
